# Four evaluation questions: Was it completed, is it robust, why did it work, and what did it cost?

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability.md) · English

Updated 2026-11-04 · 44 topic entries / 7 representative comparisons

GAIA scores final answers. AgentPerturb tests single-target input changes; User Proxy Bench checks whether simulators bypass information gathering. AlphaDiana tracks failures and retries; HDA decomposes harness gains, and selective evaluation bounds automated judge error. High scores only become interpretable after these protocols are explicit.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

!!! note "How to read this card"

    The table compares representative methods. It is not a shared-benchmark leaderboard. Teaching examples are not measured results.

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Task success can conceal a change in what is being measured

GAIA-style exact answers show whether deliverables match references. If a simulated user reveals information the agent was supposed to ask for, the task can succeed while testing less information gathering. User Proxy Bench separates UFS from reward. AgentPerturb likewise requires unchanged intent and solvability: blaming agents for broken tasks does not measure robustness. Good evaluation controls the task and visibility, not just whether scores move.

Sources: [GAIA](../../../../agent-research/2311.12983-gaia/README-en.md) · [UserProxyBench: Evaluating LLM User Simulators for Agent Benchmarks and Training](../../../../agent-research/2609.38043-userproxybench/README-en.md) · [AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations](../../../../agent-research/2610.21624-agent-perturb/README-en.md)

### Paired designs still need failure records and attribution conditions

AlphaDiana preserves logical sample counts across retries, sums attempt costs, and separates successful execution from grading. HDA aligns four arms itemwise, controls budgets, uses human-reviewed neutralization, and establishes gains before attribution. Selective evaluation clusters repeated trajectories by task instead of treating them as independent calibration. These govern interpretation without converting missing grades, unseen shortcuts, or uncovered tasks into verified outcomes.

Sources: [AlphaDiana: A Measurement System for Agents in Verifiable Reasoning Tasks](../../../../agent-research/2610.20675-alpha-diana/README-en.md) · [Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution](../../../../agent-research/2610.22466-harness-decomposition/README-en.md) · [Certified Selective Automation of LLM Agent Evaluation](../../../../agent-research/2609.34320-certified-selective-eval/README-en.md)

### When an unsolvable task is valid evaluation rather than artificially broken robustness

AgentPerturb preserves the original objective and solvability after perturbation, avoiding manufactured failures. AgentHeal instead labels genuine unrecoverability as its own regime, assessing honest abstention, diagnosis, and compliance without demanding nonexistent answers. Recoverable cases still require preferring exact copies or disclosing version differences. GAIA-style final-answer correctness does not replace source and process conditions. Answer rates, recovery rates, and reliability stay distinct only when expected behavior and denominators are explicit for each regime.

Sources: [AgentHeal: Evaluating Goal-Preserving Resource Recovery of Web Agents under Access Barriers](../../../../agent-research/2610.39234-agentheal/README-en.md) · [AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations](../../../../agent-research/2610.21624-agent-perturb/README-en.md) · [GAIA](../../../../agent-research/2311.12983-gaia/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### Why can User Proxy Bench reject evaluation even when a tool task succeeds, and why require solvability after AgentPerturb changes? {#cross-success-versus-proxy-fidelity}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** User Proxy Bench checks disclosure contracts: giving private fields unprompted bypasses clarification ability. AgentPerturb preserves goal, executability, and solvability so impossible tasks do not masquerade as robustness losses. Final accuracy measures delivery; these protocols separately constrain excess assistance and excess disruption.

    **Illustrative example:** Providing an order number up front skips asking for it. Removing the number and forbidding clarification is also an unfair task.

    Sources: [GAIA](../../../../agent-research/2311.12983-gaia/README-en.md) · [UserProxyBench: Evaluating LLM User Simulators for Agent Benchmarks and Training](../../../../agent-research/2609.38043-userproxybench/README-en.md) · [AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations](../../../../agent-research/2610.21624-agent-perturb/README-en.md)

### If the perturbed grader fails, the clean arm is correct, and there are two retries, how do AgentPerturb and AlphaDiana avoid flattering scores? {#cross-missing-pairs-and-retries}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** AgentPerturb computes paired differences on matching doubly scored items and still reports coverage and unknown bounds over all requests. AlphaDiana keeps retries under one logical sample, chooses latest rather than best, and sums all known attempt costs. Missing grades or tokens must not be fabricated into full success cost.

    **Illustrative example:** Three costly attempts ending with grader failure cannot be reduced to one prior success or removed from the planned denominator.

    Sources: [AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations](../../../../agent-research/2610.21624-agent-perturb/README-en.md) · [AlphaDiana: A Measurement System for Agents in Verifiable Reasoning Tasks](../../../../agent-research/2610.20675-alpha-diana/README-en.md)

### Why do remaining HDA gains after neutralizing shortcuts and passing a selective-evaluation risk certificate support different conclusions? {#cross-gain-attribution-versus-risk-certificate}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** HDA compares four arms and attributes residual gain after compute and detected shortcuts, which can still include unknown shortcuts and does not prove transfer. Selective evaluation bounds error in an automated region using calibration clusters; it does not explain why a harness improved. Both require task scope and statistical units.

    **Illustrative example:** A judge meeting its regional error bound does not show the agent improved through reasoning. Remaining gains after removing one shortcut do not ensure judges transfer to another domain.

    Sources: [Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution](../../../../agent-research/2610.22466-harness-decomposition/README-en.md) · [Certified Selective Automation of LLM Agent Evaluation](../../../../agent-research/2609.34320-certified-selective-eval/README-en.md)

### Why can AgentHeal reward abstention on unrecoverable tasks while AgentPerturb cannot arbitrarily break tasks until they are unsolvable? {#cross-unrecoverable-is-a-different-contract}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Their predefined objectives differ. AgentPerturb measures paired robustness under the same solvable objective. AgentHeal measures resource recovery, explicitly distinguishing recoverable and unrecoverable cases; the latter require diagnosis and honest stopping or user assistance. Such abstention is not final-answer accuracy, and an aggregate score must not conceal different regimes.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: when the only file disappears without a lawful backup, describing the barrier instead of fabricating content is a reliability success. Requiring the original number on that same condition as a perturbation task instead breaks the question.

    Sources: [AgentHeal: Evaluating Goal-Preserving Resource Recovery of Web Agents under Access Barriers](../../../../agent-research/2610.39234-agentheal/README-en.md) · [AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations](../../../../agent-research/2610.21624-agent-perturb/README-en.md) · [GAIA](../../../../agent-research/2311.12983-gaia/README-en.md)

## Update log {#updates}

Updates record new approaches, changed trade-offs, and follow-up evidence.

Distinguished the exact-copy intersection from the other-version subset condition, with gold annotations visible only to evaluators.
